title: Relative factorization of group-product units by the identity axes
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:G\to S$ a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with geometrically connected fibres and identity $e$. A commutative group scheme has addition, inverse and identity satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume either that $p$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], or that $S$ is reduced, meaning that all its local rings have no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For $n\geq1$, put $P_n=G\times_S\cdots\times_SG$ with $n$ factors [def-pc-fibre-product], let $p_n:P_n\to S$ be its structure morphism, let $\pi_i:P_n\to G$ be projection, and let $a_i:G\to P_n$ insert its argument in coordinate $i$ and $e$ in all other coordinates. Write $e_n:S\to P_n$ for the all-identity section. For every unit $u\in\Gamma(P_n,\mathcal O_{P_n})^\times$ (a global regular function with a multiplicative inverse), there is an equality of regular functions on $P_n$,
$$u=p_n^*(e_n^*u)^{1-n}\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i^*(a_i^*u).$$
The star on functions denotes the pullback of regular functions along a scheme morphism. In particular, if $a_i^*u=1$ for every $i$, then $u=1$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79), and Remark 12.50 (geometric Rosenlicht input). Agent relative formulation: reduced smooth source permits checking identities on geometric fibres; proper case follows from universal structure-sheaf pushforward (Stacks Tag 0E0L, perfect-lemma-proper-flat-geom-red-connected).

proof.text: Put $c=e_n^*u$ and $u_i=a_i^*u$, all units since pullback preserves multiplication and inverses. Define the unit $v=u\,p_n^*(c^{n-1})\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_i^*(u_i^{-1})$ on $P_n$. For a fixed $j$, the fibre-product identities give $\pi_j a_j=\mathrm{id}_G$, $\pi_i a_j=ep$ for $i\ne j$, $p_n a_j=p$ and $e^*u_i=c$. Consequently $a_j^*v=u_jp^*(c^{n-1})u_j^{-1}\prod_{i\ne j}p^*(c^{-1})=1$. Also $e_n^*v=e^*a_j^*v=1$, since $n\ge1$. It remains to prove that every such axis-trivial unit $v$ equals $1$. For $n=1$, $a_1=\mathrm{id}_G$ already proves this; the arguments below also include that case.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79): normalization at the chosen identity points; agent finite-product normalization

proof.text: First suppose $p$ is proper. Smoothness implies flatness [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and geometrically reduced fibres [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Finite presentation and geometric connectedness are hypotheses. Thus [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections] applies to $p$ and gives the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T\simeq(p_T)_*\mathcal O_{G_T}$ for every $T\to S$, including nonreduced $T$. Set $P_0=S$. The projection $q_m:P_m=P_{m-1}\times_SG\to P_{m-1}$ is such a base change. Taking global sections gives a bijective pullback $q_m^*: \Gamma(P_{m-1},\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(P_m,\mathcal O)$. Iterating, $v=p_n^*d$ for a unique $d\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. Applying $e_n^*$ yields $d=e_n^*v=1$, hence $v=1$. This uses universal pushforward for $p$ itself; no reducedness of $S$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0E0L, lemma-proper-flat-geom-red-connected; smooth inputs: Tags 01VF and 056T

proof.text: Now suppose $S$ is reduced. We show by induction that every $P_m$ is reduced, starting with $P_0=S$. The projection $q_m:P_m\to P_{m-1}$ is a base change of $p$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Unpack the affine-local smooth-ring definition in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: around any point of $P_m$ choose affine opens $U\to V$ for $q_m$ with $R=\mathcal O(V)\to A=\mathcal O(U)$ smooth. By induction and [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $R$ is reduced. Then $A$ is reduced by [lem-sfb-smooth-algebra-over-reduced-ring] (Tag 033B, which does not assume $R$ Noetherian). Localizations of a reduced ring are reduced: if $(a/s)^N=0$, some denominator $t$ kills $a^N$, so $(ta)^N=0$, whence $ta=0$ and $a/s=0$. Thus the local rings on this affine cover are reduced. Thus $P_m$ is reduced. This proves the claim for arbitrary reduced $S$, without adding a local Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up; affine-local smoothness Tag 01V5; reducedness Tag 01J1

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $F$ and a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}F\to S$. Write $H=G_F$ and $H_m=P_m\times_S\operatorname{Spec}F$, with $H_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$. The maps $H_m\to H_{m-1}$ are base changes of $p$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Their fibres are base extensions of fibres of $p$, hence geometrically connected by hypothesis, and $H_m$ is nonempty because of its identity point. Inductively apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to these maps, beginning with the integral normal field spectrum. It gives that each $H_m$ is integral with integrally closed local rings. Each is of finite type over $F$: $H\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite presentation, hence of finite type, and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] gives the finite-type assertion inductively. Finally $H$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. Each $H_m$ is separated as well: in $H_m\times_FH_m$, pull back the closed diagonal of $H$ along each pair of coordinate projections, using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The intersection is closed, locally defined by the sum of these ideals. Its functor of points consists exactly of pairs of equal tuples, so it is the diagonal of $H_m$. Thus $H_{m-1}$ and $H$ meet all hypotheses of Rosenlicht's product lemma for $m\ge2$.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; normal connected source input from lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core; permanence Tags 01VB, 01T3, 01T4, 01KU and 01JY

proof.text: On the schemes $H_m$, prove by induction on $m\ge1$ that a unit $w$ whose identity-axis restrictions are all $1$ equals $1$. The case $m=1$ is the identity restriction. For $m\ge2$, apply [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-product-unit-factorization] to $X=H_{m-1}$ and $Y=H$ with points $e_{m-1}$ and $e$. Its displayed identity gives, as regular functions, $w(x,y)=w(x,e)w(e_{m-1},y)w(e_{m-1},e)^{-1}$. The unit $w(x,e)$ has every one of its $m-1$ axis restrictions equal to $1$, so equals $1$ by induction. The last-axis condition says $w(e_{m-1},y)=1$, and restriction to the identity gives $w(e_{m-1},e)=1$. Hence $w=1$. Apply this to the pullback $v_F$: pullback preserves the axis identities from Step 1. Thus $v_F=1$ for every such $F\to S$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79), and Remark 12.50; elementary induction on the number of factors

proof.text: Let $h=v-1$. For any $x\in P_n$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P_n$ factors through $P_n\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ by the fibre-product universal property. Step 5 for the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ shows the image of $h(x)\in\kappa(x)$ in $\Omega$ is zero. Since a field extension is injective, $h(x)=0$. On each affine open $U\subseteq P_n$, [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent] applies to $h|_U$, since affine schemes are quasi-compact and the section vanishes in every residue field. It is nilpotent. Step 3 and [def-pc-reduced-scheme] say $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is reduced, so $h|_U=0$. These equalities on an affine cover imply $h=0$ by the sheaf axiom, i.e. $v=1$. This is why fibrewise testing is valid here; no assertion that geometric fibres detect nilpotents on an arbitrary base is made.

source.place: Tag 01J1, lemma-reduced; residue-field vanishing and nilpotence as in More on Morphisms Tag 03GY, lemma-stein-universally-closed, proof

proof.text: In either case $v=1$. Substituting the expression of Step 1 and multiplying by the inverse unit factors gives $u=p_n^*(c^{1-n})\prod_i\pi_i^*(a_i^*u)$, the required equality. If every $a_i^*u=1$, then $c=e^*a_1^*u=1$ and this formula gives $u=1$. The proof also covers $S=\varnothing$: every section ring is then the zero ring and the displayed unit identities are unique.
